issue.title: [Bug]: A message to a running conversation waits for the current tool call to finish

labels.name: repo-08ff7f38
labels.description: For bugs, affects only non-mainstream cases, or is annoying but with a clear workaround.

issue.body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Related: #6553 (the same lock, from the angle of executor saturation). That issue is about the server wedging. This one is about latency the person sees even when nothing wedges.

### Bug Description

`POST /api/conversations/{id}/events` to a conversation whose agent is running a long tool call does not save the message until that tool call ends. `LocalConversation.send_message()` takes the conversation's state lock (`with self._state:`), and a live run holds that lock for the whole step, tool execution included. So the person's message, and anything the UI does after it, waits behind the command.

In an end-to-end Projects run (#6602 at `67c1038`, Canvas #19495), "Wait, actually: …" was sent to a worker while its terminal ran a 7-minute `pytest`. Canvas showed "Sending…" for about 6.5 minutes. The message reached the agent only when the command ended. With the terminal tool's long timeouts (agents here run suites with `timeout 3000`), a correction can wait up to 50 minutes.

This is not specific to Projects. Projects just makes it common, because the person drops into a busy worker to redirect it.

### Expected Behavior

The message is saved and acknowledged at once. The agent sees it at its next step, or the person can choose to interrupt the running tool.

### Actual Behavior

The request does not return until the running tool call ends, and the message is not in the event log until then.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a conversation whose agent runs a terminal command that takes a few minutes (for example `sleep 300`).
2. While it runs, `POST /api/conversations/{id}/events` with `run: true`.
3. The request returns only when the command ends.

### Possible directions

- Append user messages through a path that does not need the step's state lock, for example a queue that the run drains at the start of its next step.
- Or accept the message at once and expose "message queued behind a running tool", so UIs can offer "interrupt and send".

### OpenHands Version

main, plus #6602 at `67c1038`

comment.body: My agents filed this issue, after a few hours of running live testing… I know it has come up occasionally in the past, but TBH personally I don’t think it matters a lot, nor is it clear to me how it would help my agents since the user didn’t interrupt. The user can interrupt with the Stop button. 🤔

issue.title: [Feature]: Keep DigitalOcean connected: stay signed in, sign in with DigitalOcean, agents and new devices

labels.name: repo-a68fbf55
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: repo-a68fbf55
labels.description: Minor or narrowly scoped bug with low user or operational impact.

labels.name: repo-a68fbf55
labels.description: Scoped for contribution. Managed by issue-readiness-check.yml.

issue.body:
### Problem or Motivation

In the web build, the DigitalOcean sign-in lives only in the server's memory. Every Canvas restart signs the user out, and they have to paste a token again (reproduced with `control-openhands restart` on 2026-10-19: `getAuthState` returned no connections and the sign-in form came back).

Other gaps around the same connection:

- The browser can only take a personal access token. There is no "Sign in with DigitalOcean" outside the desktop app.
- An agent that already holds the Canvas session key can list DigitalOcean agents through `/mars/rpc`, but it cannot talk to a session: the proxy refuses the WebSocket upgrade (401) unless a header or cookie is present, and the sandbox prep runs only in the browser.
- A second device (an iPad on the same network) has to type the session key before it can use the Mac's DigitalOcean connection.

### Desired Behavior

The design is at https://enyst.github.io/arch/keep-digitalocean-connected.html. The short version is: people sign in; agents use keys.

- As a user, I add a DigitalOcean backend and sign in with my DigitalOcean account. I don't paste a key. A personal access token stays available as a fallback.
- As a user, I restart Canvas and I'm still signed in. The panel names my team and says where the sign-in is kept, for example "Saved in the macOS Keychain on studio.local". When nothing can keep it, the panel says so.
- As a user with an iPad, I scan a QR code shown on my Mac and the iPad can use the same DigitalOcean backend. I don't type a key there.
- As an agent with the Canvas session key, I can start a session in DigitalOcean and talk to its agent server, using the team that's active in the UI.

The sign-in is saved on the machine that runs Canvas: the macOS Keychain or Secret Service when there is one, otherwise a file encrypted with `OH_SECRET_KEY`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a Canvas restart, a browser that was signed in to DigitalOcean is still signed in and lists the team's agents without re-entering anything.
- [ ] The DigitalOcean panel shows the team (and account email) and where the sign-in is kept, or warns that it will not survive a restart.
- [ ] Signing out removes the saved sign-in from the host.
- [ ] In the web build, "Sign in with DigitalOcean" completes and the connection keeps working after the one-hour access token expires.
- [ ] An agent with the session key can open a DigitalOcean session's agent-server socket through the Canvas proxy (first-message auth) and run a conversation there.
- [ ] A second browser can be paired from a QR code shown in a signed-in browser, without typing the session key.

### Alternatives Considered

- A native keychain module (`@napi-rs/keyring`) instead of the OS tools (`/usr/bin/security`, `secret-tool`). It means a native build per platform; it stays the fallback.
- Separate DigitalOcean keys for agents. Agents already hold the session key, so they reuse it for now. User-created admin keys are a follow-up.
- DigitalOcean login on a new device instead of pairing. It needs an HTTPS return address and an owner check; pairing needs neither. It comes later.

### Additional Context

The work goes in as stacked PRs, one per step: stay signed in, then sign in with DigitalOcean, then agents, then pairing.

<!-- openhands-ai-triage:start -->
---
## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Scope: four sequential changes to the DigitalOcean/MARS bridge, all owned by this repository. Root `AGENTS.md` gives `OpenHands/OpenHands` "Agent Canvas UI, frontend state, backend selection, frontend service integration, and local-stack orchestration", and `src/api/mars/AGENTS.md` documents exactly the behavior the issue reports: the bridge lives in `scripts/mars-*.mjs` / `src/api/mars/`, web-build credentials are in-memory, the `/mars` cookie secret is random per process, `canUseOAuth` is `false`, and the proxy refuses an event-socket upgrade without a header or cookie. The linked design document is the authoritative scope for the four steps:

1. Stay signed in — persist the saved sign-in on the Canvas host through a `SecretStore` (macOS Keychain / Secret Service, else an encrypted file keyed by `OH_SECRET_KEY`, else an explicit run-only state), derive the bridge cookie from the session key, keep the saved backend identity, and show the team and where the sign-in is kept.
2. Sign in with DigitalOcean — authorization-code flow with PKCE and refresh on the Canvas origin, with the personal access token kept as a fallback.
3. Agents — let a caller holding the Canvas session key open and drive a DigitalOcean session through the proxy (first-message socket auth, host-side sandbox preparation, documented calls).
4. New devices — pair a second browser from a QR code / link shown in a signed-in browser, without typing the session key.

Non-goals (from the issue and the design document): no new key types, roles or permission tiers; no separate DigitalOcean keys for agents (they reuse the session key); no DigitalOcean login on a new device (pairing is the chosen route); user-created admin keys, the desktop app's network-listening setting, and agents that cannot reach the Canvas host (they use their own DigitalOcean token directly) are recorded follow-ups, not part of this work. The desktop-app move onto the one bridge and the choice between a native keyring module and the OS tools are implementation decisions inside steps 1–2, not separate scope.

The design document's open questions — the shipped OAuth client ID, the granted scopes and refresh-token lifetime, and whether DigitalOcean accepts a host-registered HTTPS callback — are external confirmations that gate steps 2 and 4. They are not unresolved product design decisions, so they do not block development of the scope above.

### Acceptance Criteria

Step 1 — stay signed in
- [ ] In the web build, a browser signed in to DigitalOcean is still authenticated after a Canvas restart: `getAuthState()` returns the same connection(s) with a non-null active connection, and the panel lists the team's OpenHands agents without re-entering anything.
- [ ] The saved sign-in survives a host restart and a reboot when a supported OS store is present (macOS Keychain, or Secret Service that survives reboot); a store that forgets on reboot is not reported as "saved".
- [ ] On a host with no usable store, the panel and the Managed Agents account line name the actual storage ("Saved encrypted on this server", naming `OH_SECRET_KEY`), and run-only mode is an explicit labelled state that warns it will not survive a restart. No token is ever written to disk in the clear.
- [ ] Every signed-in view names the active team (and the account email when the token may read it) and where the sign-in is kept; when nothing can keep it, the same view says it will not survive a restart.
- [ ] Signing out removes the saved secret and its metadata record from the host, and a later `getAuthState()` returns no connection for it. Signing out does not delete any DigitalOcean session.
- [ ] The bridge cookie value is derived from the host session key rather than a per-process random, so a browser's cookie stays valid across a normal restart; rotating the session key invalidates it.

Step 2 — sign in with DigitalOcean
- [ ] In the web build, "Sign in with DigitalOcean" completes the authorization-code + PKCE flow on the Canvas origin, and the connection keeps working after the one-hour access token expires, by renewing with the saved refresh token.
- [ ] Renewal is single-flight per connection and the new token pair is persisted before it is used, so two tabs or two processes cannot leave the host holding a spent refresh token.
- [ ] When DigitalOcean refuses a renewal, the connection is marked needs-sign-in, the saved DigitalOcean backend and its conversation selection stay intact, and the UI offers re-sign-in instead of a generic key form. The generic key form never rewrites a DigitalOcean backend.
- [ ] A cancelled, expired (past 10 minutes), replayed, or state-mismatched callback leaves the existing connection unchanged and grants no host access.
- [ ] A personal access token remains available as a fallback and continues to sign in and persist like today.

Step 3 — agents
- [ ] An event-socket upgrade on `/mars/sessions/<id>` with no cookie or key header is accepted when its first message is the SDK's auth frame within 10 seconds; the key is compared in constant time and the auth frame is dropped before frames are piped to the guest. A missing or wrong key closes 4001 and opens no connection to the session.
- [ ] The connect step performs any still-needed sandbox preparation on the host, so an agent that opens a session through the bridge gets the same prepared sandbox a browser connect gets.
- [ ] An agent holding the session key can list agent configs, create a session, open a tunnel, start a conversation through the proxy, and pause the session, using the DigitalOcean team that is active in the UI.
- [ ] The Canvas session key and the `/mars` cookie never reach the guest; Canvas-only headers stay stripped.

Step 4 — new devices (pairing)
- [ ] A signed-in browser can show a QR code and a copyable link ("Add another device") whose single-use secret is carried after `#`, so it never appears in server or proxy logs; the link expires after 5 minutes.
- [ ] A second browser that opens the link gains the same access as presenting the session key, without typing the session key, and stays admitted across a restart.
- [ ] An expired or already-used link grants no access.

Cross-cutting and validation
- [ ] Plain-HTTP pages served to a non-loopback address show the unencrypted-connection warning; loopback pages do not.
- [ ] No DigitalOcean access token or refresh token appears in any RPC response, log line, URL, or `localStorage`.
- [ ] New tests cover the secret store's keychain / encrypted-file / memory backends, the derived cookie surviving a restart, the socket first-message auth (accept and 4001 reject), and pairing link single-use and expiry. Existing MARS tests pass, and `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, and `npm run build:lib` pass.
- [ ] Verified live: restart Canvas and land back in the same DigitalOcean session and conversation, comparing the backend ID, DigitalOcean session ID and connection ID before and after.

AGENT:

## Live test against a real DigitalOcean account (9 Nov)

Run on #18711's head (248c5f966, which includes #18706 and #18707), with `control-openhands launch --mars-web` and a test public OAuth client registered for the run. The approval was given on an iPad and finished by pasting the return address back.

**Worked**
- **Sign in with DigitalOcean (code + PKCE):** the panel named the team and said "Saved encrypted on vm (no keychain here)".
- **Restart:** still signed in after `control-openhands restart`.
- **Create and launch:** New Agent picked the smallest size by itself (`mars-1vcpu-1gb`). "Create and launch" created a real agent config and session, and the session was `READY` about 16 s after it was created.
- **Tunnel:** `openTunnel` connected over DigitalOcean's port-forward (`status: connected`, remote port 8000).
- **Sign out:** DigitalOcean confirmed the revoke.

**Blocked: the guest agent-server now requires a session API key**
- The guest runs agent-server 1.58.2.
  - `/alive`, `/health`, `/server_info` and `/openapi.json` answer 200.
  - Every `/api/*` route tried (`/api/settings`, `/api/conversations/search`, `/api/bash/bash_events/search`) answers `401 {"detail":"Unauthorized"}`.
- The host-side prep stopped at once, as designed: `could not prepare the sandbox: HTTP request failed (401 Unauthorized)`, and `openTunnel` reported `sandbox: "failed"`.
- The page then showed "Invalid API key" on the agent row and closed the tunnel.

**Why**
- **agent-server never makes up a key.** It enforces `X-Session-API-Key` only when whatever starts it supplies one: `SESSION_API_KEY` or `OH_SESSION_API_KEYS_0` at boot, or `POST /api/init` for pre-started servers. The rule is the same in 1.57.0, 1.58.2 and 1.60.1, so DigitalOcean's `openhands` template now gives the guest a key.
- **`main` assumes there is none.** Since #18549 (16 Oct), `src/api/mars/mars-tunnel-backend.ts` sends `MARS_GUEST_API_KEY = ""`, with the comment "The in-guest agent-server's session key is set by the sandbox template, not by us." So released Canvas should get the same 401 on new sessions. That's from reading the code; I haven't run `main` against DigitalOcean.
- **When it changed:** after 25 Oct, the release date of 1.58.2, the version the guest runs. It may have come with that template update or later.
- **Nowhere to get the key from:** the session record (`GET /v2/agents/sessions/{id}`) has no key field. The [OpenHands how-to](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/managed-agents/agent-harness-runtime/how-to/run-openhands-agent/) and [port-forward](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/managed-agents/agent-harness-runtime/how-to/forward-ports/) pages don't mention one, and the [release notes](https://docs.digitalocean.com/release-notes/agent-harness-runtime/) say nothing after 12 Oct.

issue.title: [Bug]: A message to a running conversation waits for the current tool call to finish

labels.name: repo-08ff7f38
labels.description: For bugs, affects only non-mainstream cases, or is annoying but with a clear workaround.

issue.body:
### Is there an existing issue for the same bug?

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Related: #6553 (the same lock, from the angle of executor saturation). That issue is about the server wedging. This one is about latency the person sees even when nothing wedges.

### Bug Description

`POST /api/conversations/{id}/events` to a conversation whose agent is running a long tool call does not save the message until that tool call ends. `LocalConversation.send_message()` takes the conversation's state lock (`with self._state:`), and a live run holds that lock for the whole step, tool execution included. So the person's message, and anything the UI does after it, waits behind the command.

In an end-to-end Projects run (#6602 at `67c1038`, Canvas #19495), "Wait, actually: …" was sent to a worker while its terminal ran a 7-minute `pytest`. Canvas showed "Sending…" for about 6.5 minutes. The message reached the agent only when the command ended. With the terminal tool's long timeouts (agents here run suites with `timeout 3000`), a correction can wait up to 50 minutes.

This is not specific to Projects. Projects just makes it common, because the person drops into a busy worker to redirect it.

### Expected Behavior

The message is saved and acknowledged at once. The agent sees it at its next step, or the person can choose to interrupt the running tool.

### Actual Behavior

The request does not return until the running tool call ends, and the message is not in the event log until then.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a conversation whose agent runs a terminal command that takes a few minutes (for example `sleep 300`).
2. While it runs, `POST /api/conversations/{id}/events` with `run: true`.
3. The request returns only when the command ends.

### Possible directions

- Append user messages through a path that does not need the step's state lock, for example a queue that the run drains at the start of its next step.
- Or accept the message at once and expose "message queued behind a running tool", so UIs can offer "interrupt and send".

### OpenHands Version

main, plus #6602 at `67c1038`

<!-- Keep this PR as draft until it is ready for review. -->

HUMAN:

<!-- Human contributors: add a short note about your testing. -->

I've ran `npm run dev:mock` to test the virtualization shell. Verified smooth scrolling, streaming message updates, and short-chat fallback behavior. Also all unit tests passed (`npm test`).

---

AGENT:

Virtualizes the conversation message list so cost stops growing with session
length, and removes a quadratic scan in the grouping pass that ran on every
render.

### Review follow-up (all-hands-bot, head `f591fa6`)

The bot requested changes on the same two points the Devin flags raised, both
now addressed on real infrastructure rather than the mock seam:

- **Blocking — production-facing evidence.** The prior "real browser" numbers
  came from the DEV-only `window.__OH_EVENT_STORE__` seam and a Devin-only
  `?virtualize=0` flag. They are replaced below with a **real
  `openhands-agent-server`** (v1.53.0) driving real persisted events, and with a
  genuine **base-vs-head** build pair — no mock API, no mock LLM, no DEV-only
  flag. The `?virtualize=0` escape hatch is now deleted (§ Notes).
- **Blocking — base/released before.** The "before" is now the base commit
  `3f98684` built and served on the same agent-server, not the head forced onto
  the plain path.
- **Non-blocking — threshold divergence.** The 150-row choice (vs the ~50 first
  sketched in #18102) is justified in-source at `VIRTUALIZATION_THRESHOLD`.
- **Non-blocking — DEV seam.** Removed in `ea82ccb`; `messages.tsx` has a single
  rendering decision and no comparison branch.

### The reported symptom

> “Chatnya sudah sangat panjang; ketika di-refresh ke halaman chat, aplikasinya
> me-render jendela dari chat awal sampai chat akhir — padahal harusnya hanya
> menampilkan beberapa jendela chat terakhir — dan makin lama makin lambat.”

That is exactly the mechanism above, with one nuance worth stating plainly: a
cold load only fetches the last 50 events
(`INITIAL_HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE`), so the list does not start at 800. What grows is
what is *retained*: every older page the user scrolls into, plus every event the
session streams, stays mounted and is re-rendered on the next refresh, re-render
or append. Only the last screenful needs to be in the DOM; the rest should be
represented by the virtualizer's measured offsets.

### Evidence — real backend, base vs head

Setup (both columns identical except for the build):

- **Backend:** `openhands-agent-server` v1.53.0 on `127.0.0.1:18801`, reached
  through the ingress on `127.0.0.1:18800`. All events are persisted to disk and
  served over the real `/api/conversations/<id>/events/search` pagination path.
- **Conversation:** one saved conversation with **417 real events** — 16 from a
  live agent run (three `shell` commands, which produce an expandable
  action/observation group) plus seeded padding so the history is long enough to
  virtualize.
- **Frontends:** the **base** commit `3f98684` and the **head** build, each
  served as a real production build (`static-server.mjs`) proxied to the same
  agent-server; driven by Chromium 153 via Playwright. Same viewport, same
  conversation, same backend.

**Temporal behaviors the bot asked to see** (`data-testid="chat-scroll-container"`):

1. **Scroll to top still lazily loads older pages, and content stays put.** On
   each `scrollTop = 0` the `loading-older-events` spinner appears and a page
   merges. The topmost visible user bubble measures within ~8 px of the same
   pixel offset before and after the prepend (scroll anchoring holds) —
   `anchorStationary: true`, `sawSpinner: true`.
2. **A streamed tail event autoscrolls only while pinned to the bottom.** With
   the view at the bottom, a freshly POSTed event follows (distance-to-bottom
   stays ~0: `scrollTop 15470 → 15562`, `scrollHeight 16284 → 16376`). With the
   view scrolled up, the same event arrives and `scrollTop` is unchanged
   (`5536 → 5536`) while the list grows — it does not steal scroll.
3. **An expanded group grows its row and the rows below re-measure.** Toggling
   the real action/observation group increases `scrollHeight`
   (`20768 → 20918`) and subsequent rows re-lay out instead of overlapping.

**DOM cost, same conversation, stepped through the real backfill** (read live):

| backfill step (successive real pages) | base `3f98684` DOM nodes | head DOM nodes | base rows | head rows |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------- | --------- | --------- |
| 1 (75 events)                         | 1,225                    | 1,233          | 0         | 0         |
| 2 (100 events)                        | 1,525                    | 1,533          | 0         | 0         |
| 3 (125 events)                        | 1,825                    | 1,833          | 0         | 0         |
| 4 (150 events)                        | 2,125                    | 2,133          | 0         | 0         |
| 5                                    | 2,425                    | **959**        | 0         | **25**    |
| 6                                    | 2,725                    | **959**        | 0         | **25**    |

Below the threshold both paths are byte-for-byte similar; once the rendered-row
count crosses it, the head switches to a bounded mounted window (~25 rows / 959
nodes) while the base keeps adding ~11 nodes per event with no ceiling. The raw
JSON for both runs is committed under the artifacts below.

### Video / screenshots (real backend)

**Video (recommended): `17820-temporal-before-after.gif` / `.mp4`.** Two real
builds, one saved 417-event conversation, one agent-server. First half: base
`3f98684` plain list (red badge). Second half: head virtualized list (green
badge). It walks the three temporal behaviors above — lazy older-page load with
stationary content, tail autoscroll gated on the bottom, and an expanded group
re-measuring the rows below.

([mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/analisaperlengkapan/OpenHands/pr-assets/pr-assets/live-virt-17820/17820-temporal-before-after.mp4))

  children) and seeds the virtualizer through `buildInitialMeasurements`, so the
  shell's total height — and the scroll offset — is unchanged by the switch
  instead of collapsing to the flat 120px estimate.
- **P2 — "scroll to bottom" stopped short.** `shouldAdjustScrollOnSizeChange`
  keeps bottom alignment when a tall row at or below the viewport is measured
  while the reader is pinned to the bottom (`scrollHeight - delta` gives the
  pre-change height).
- **P2 — "Branch from here" lost its observer on scroll-away.** Navigation,
  draft restoration and the error toast moved into `useForkConversation`'s
  mutation-level callbacks, which fire even when the invoking row has been
  virtualized out mid-flight.
- **P2 — remaining expanders collapsed after scroll-out/back.** Long user
  prompts, code output, skill-knowledge cards, profile cards, critic details and
  error details now persist their expansion by row + control, using a new
  event-scoped `useEventExpansionKey` so several cards sharing one row key
  independently.
- **P2 — virtual rows lacked the flex-column layout.** Each row re-establishes
  `flex flex-col`, so the user bubble's `self-end` right alignment holds.
- **P2 — empty planning rows left blank scroll space.** Planning observations
  that render nothing are filtered out of the virtualized row set.
- **P2 — reject cards shared expansion state.** The reject card gets an
  event-specific `expansionId`.
- **P3 — `getItemKey` identity churn.** `getItemKey` is memoized against the row
  set so the measurement cache is not invalidated on every render.

Tests: new `scroll-anchoring.test.ts` and `use-fork-conversation.test.tsx`;
`messages-virtualization.test.tsx` covers the height seed and the flex-column
row layout. Full suite 9,064 passed; `tsc`, ESLint and `npm run build` green.

### Review follow-up (Codex on `db345d0`, head `72bd107d`)

A third review round (Codex on `db345d0`) raised two P2 correctness issues on the
virtualized path; both are fixed in `72bd107d`:

- **P2 — bottom pinning judged after the height correction.** TanStack 3.11.3
  calls `shouldAdjustScrollPositionOnItemSizeChange` *before* it updates its size
  cache and before React re-renders the shell, so `scrollHeight` still holds the
  pre-change height. Subtracting `delta` compared against a height that was never
  laid out and mislabelled a reader who had scrolled up as pinned
  (`scrollTop=500`, `clientHeight=400`, `scrollHeight=1000`; a visible row at 600
  growing 100→300 jumped the reader from 500 to 600). `shouldAdjustScrollOnSizeChange`
  now compares against the element's current `scrollHeight` directly, and
  `scroll-anchoring.test.ts` covers growth below the viewport top while the
  reader is away from the bottom.
- **P2 — hidden planning rows took their model entries with them.** `/model` and
  profile switches can be anchored to a planning observation
  (`getLastRenderableEventId` accepts observation events), so once a later plan
  observation became the phase preview the earlier row was filtered out and its
  entry disappeared in long conversations. The `renderedItems` filter now retains
  rows whose ids are in `modelAnchorIds`; the event content still renders null
  while the entry shows. `messages-model-messages.test.tsx` drives the real
  `Messages`/`ModelMessages` past the threshold and fails without the change.

Also merged `upstream/main` (`44d8f8f7`) into the branch; the three conflicts
(`messages.tsx`, `chat-interface.tsx`, `mock-llm-ui-regressions.spec.ts`) kept
both the virtualization work and upstream's changes. Full suite 9,572 passed;
`tsc`, ESLint and `npm run build` green.

---

### Review follow-up (long-chat switch, head `9e800a2e`)

A follow-up review of the seed path found that a long-chat switch could still
lose the reader's place. Both causes are fixed in `9e800a2e`.

**1. Row margins were left out of the seed.** A plain row's wrapper is
`display: contents`, so the row's extent is the span of its children, and a
bounding rectangle is the *border* box: it omits the children's vertical margins
(the user/agent bubble's `mt-6` = 24px, the last child's `mb-4` = 16px). A
virtual row's own box *does* contain them, so the seed was systematically shorter
than the list it replaced and the browser clamped `scrollTop` toward the bottom.
Rows are now measured by the height they actually occupy
(`occupiedRowHeight`), the same terms `measureElement` reports for a virtual row.

Verified against real CSS in Chromium, not only mocked rectangles:

| | 3 rows + gaps |
|---|---|
| Plain list `scrollHeight` | 760px |
| Seed from bounding rectangles (before) | 712px — **48px short** |
| Seed from occupied height (after) | 760px |

and for a single row with a 232px border box and a 24px top margin, the occupied
height is 248px — exactly the virtual row's box height.

**2. The cache could go stale without the row set changing.** A reader expands a
group, or async content settles, and a later append crosses the threshold; the
cache still held the collapsed height, so the shell came up short again. A
`ResizeObserver` now re-measures the row that resized, in place. (Measuring at
unmount is not possible: React detaches refs before layout-effect cleanup, so
`ref.current` is already `null` there — confirmed with a probe.)

Tests: `scroll-anchoring.test.ts` covers `measurePlainRow`;
`messages-virtualization.test.tsx` seeds across the threshold with margins in
play, and grows an off-screen row with no re-render and asserts the seed picks up
its new height. Both fail without the fixes. Full suite 9,576 passed; `tsc`,
ESLint and Prettier green.

Follow-up on the same review: `occupiedRowHeight` had been exported only so a
unit test could call it, while production reaches it through `measurePlainRow`.
`bccaf386` drops the export and asserts the margin behaviour through
`measurePlainRow`, the path the component actually takes.

---

## Why

For long conversations every event ever loaded stayed mounted in the DOM, so a
refresh or a streamed append re-rendered the whole history — ~11 DOM nodes per
event (~12k nodes at ~1,050 events, ~24k at ~2,050). Scroll, style recalculation
and input latency grew with session length. Reported in #18102; superseded the
stale #12707.

## Summary

- Virtualize the grouped rows (`RenderedItem[]`, the `groupEvents()` output —
  not raw events) with `@tanstack/react-virtual`, so grouping, thought hoisting
  and the streaming tail keep their existing semantics and stable keys. Rows are
  measured from the live DOM so code blocks, images and expanded output correct
  the offsets instead of drifting. Below 150 rows the plain list renders
  verbatim, so short conversations are byte-identical.
- `Messages` now takes the scroll *element* (`scrollParent`) instead of a ref.
  A ref owned by `chat-interface` never re-renders the child when it is
  populated, which left the virtualizer permanently detached — a bug the
  benchmark caught (the first cut still rendered all 4,100 rows on mount).
  `undefined` means "no virtualization context" (shared/read-only views keep the
  plain list); `null` means "container exists, element not mounted yet", which
  renders the virtualized shell instead of paying for a full first render.
- Give the virtualized shell `flex-shrink: 0`. Its rows are absolutely
  positioned, so the shell has no in-flow content; as a flex child of the
  scrolling column it was shrunk back to the viewport, which clamped the scroll
  height to one viewport and pinned the virtualizer to the tail — earlier
  messages could never be scrolled into view. Caught by the real-browser run
  above (scroll height 3,464 px clamped → 100,280 px). The virtualization test
  now asserts this contract.
- Index action events by id once per grouping (`buildActionById`) instead of
  `allEvents.find(...)` per observation, which also ran again inside
  `getThoughtSourceAction()` — quadratic on every render.

## Issue Number
Fixes #18102

### Review follow-up (VascoSch92, head `6082c99d`)

All 24 review threads are resolved. The behavioural fixes in `6082c99d`:

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| Anchor correction treated a row straddling the top edge as "above the viewport" | `anchorScrollOnItemSizeChange` now takes `{start, end}` and skips a row whose `end` is still below the offset, so a group the reader just expanded stays put. Only rows entirely above the viewport correct. |
| A box added to an existing row was never measured | The plain phase runs a `MutationObserver` over each `[data-row-key]` wrapper's child list, so a `/model` card, a secret card, or a pending bubble joining a row re-measures it and updates the height the shell is seeded from. |
| Anchored `request_secret` card unmounts inside a virtual row | Pending cards render in `trailingContent` while virtualizing. Beyond losing the typed draft, unmounting the card dropped the per-call `onSuccess` that reports the result to the agent, leaving the tool call unanswered. The plain list still renders each card next to its call. |
| Trailing bubble margin | The per-message `last:mb-4` is gone from `chat-message.tsx` and `corrective-nudge-message.tsx`, and `row-margins.ts` (plus its test) is deleted: with a per-row wrapper every bubble was `:last-child`, so the reset fought a margin that no longer served a purpose. The scroll column's `pb-12` supplies the trailing space. |
| Older-page load drift once virtualized | `chat-interface` also captures a row anchor (first row at or below the top edge + its offset) when a load starts, and a second pass after the page merges restores it once the prepended rows have measured — the height delta is taken in the commit where the new rows are still at the estimate. Helper in `scroll-anchor.ts`, unit-tested; a no-op when the row is not mounted. |
| `BOTTOM_THRESHOLD_PX` duplicated | One constant in `use-scroll-to-bottom.ts`, re-exported by `scroll-anchoring.ts`, so `isAtBottom` and the anchor correction agree. |
| Test isolation (`getComputedStyle` spy) | The virtualization file snapshots the observer globals in a top-level `beforeEach` and restores them in `afterEach`; it now passes under `--sequence.shuffle`. |

The 2026-11-02 row-scoped-expansion-key findings (thought, group, and pending-bubble
keys) were already fixed on the branch in `e69c3635` / `4398443`; their threads are
resolved with the commit that addressed them.

Verification at `6082c99d`: `npm run lint` (0 errors), `npm test` (882 files, 10086
passed), `npm run build`, and `npx tsc --noEmit` all pass.

### Follow-up (secret cache on mid-save unmount)

Moved the secrets-query invalidation out of the per-call `mutate(..., { onSuccess })`
callback and into the mutation-level success handling in `secret-form.tsx`, ordered
before `onSaved`. A `request_secret` card that unmounts mid-save (scrolled out of the
virtual window) previously completed the request but skipped invalidation, so
`useSearchSecrets` kept its five-minute cache and Settings could omit the saved secret.
A regression test unmounts the form mid-save and asserts both `["secrets-search"]` and
`["secrets"]` are invalidated.

Verification at `0deeac04d`: `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `npx vitest run` (905 files,
10618 passed | 3 skipped), `npm run build`, `npm run build:lib`, and `npm run lint`
(0 errors) all pass; upstream `main` merged clean.

## How to Test

1. `npm ci`
2. `npx vitest run __tests__/components/conversation-events/chat/` — the new
   `messages-virtualization.test.tsx` asserts a bounded row window (>150 rows),
   the plain-list fallback (<150 rows, and when no scroll container is passed),
   the full-height shell contract, and that appending an event does not remount
   an already-visible row.
3. Changed subtree: `npx vitest run __tests__/components/conversation-events/chat/ __tests__/stores/message-expansion-store.test.ts`
   → 28 files, 328 passed | 1 skipped. Full `npm test` covers the rest.
4. To see it live, start a stack (`npm run dev` or the mock-mode stack) and open
   a conversation with 150+ rendered rows: only a viewport's worth of rows should
   exist in the DOM, scrolling to the top should still load older pages without
   moving the visible content, and a streamed reply should follow the bottom only
   while the user is at the bottom.

## Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Docs / chore

## Notes

- The DEV-only `?virtualize=0` escape hatch added for the earlier clip is
  **removed** in `ea82ccb`. The before/after now films the base commit and the
  head build against the same backend, so shipped `messages.tsx` has no
  comparison branch. Sole non-production code left is the opt-in
  `BENCH_MESSAGES=1` spec, which does not run under `npm test`.
- Known limitation, also listed on #18102: not-rendered rows are absent from the
  DOM, so native Cmd+F and cross-row text selection only see mounted rows. This
  PR does not add in-conversation search; happy to add it if maintainers want it
  in scope.
- Rows are absolutely positioned with a `ROW_GAP_PX` folded into each measured
  height, because the container's flex `gap-2` does not apply to out-of-flow
  children.

issue.body:
## Bug Description
If you send a message to a conversation while its agent is running, the message can be lost. The bubble stays at "Sending…", nothing reaches the agent server, and the text later reappears as a draft in the composer.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `npm run dev` with a local agent server. Start a conversation and give it a task that runs for a while, with several tool calls.
2. While the agent is running, open the conversation, so that a new session socket opens.
3. Type a message and press Enter. The bubble shows "Sending…".
4. Within a few seconds, go to another conversation. Come back after the agent has finished.

## Actual Behavior
- No user `MessageEvent` is recorded, and no `POST /events` is made.
- The session socket `/sockets/session/{id}?after_seq=…` opens and sends 2 frames, but receives 0 frames for about 40 seconds.
- When you come back, the text is in the composer again. It is restored from `conversation-state-<id>.draftMessage`.
- Cause: the agent server subscribes a new session socket only after `_create_initial_state_sync` has the conversation's state lock. `LocalConversation.run` holds that lock for the whole agent step. Until then the server reads no inbound frames, so a frame still unread when the socket closes is dropped.

## Expected Behavior
A message sent to a running conversation is delivered, and the agent picks it up after its current step. This should hold even if you leave the page right after sending.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A message sent while the agent is running reaches the agent server, even if the person leaves the conversation right after sending.
- [ ] Canvas doesn't rely on a session socket that hasn't delivered any frame yet to carry a user message.
- [ ] Sending to an idle conversation still goes over the socket, as before.

## Related
The server side is fixed separately in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6709 (issue OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6708). This Canvas fallback also covers agent servers without that fix.

<!-- openhands-ai-triage:start -->
---
## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Reproduced against the running app (`npm run dev` with a local agent server) and confirmed against the send path: `sendMessage` in `src/contexts/conversation-websocket-context.tsx` delivers over the session socket whenever its `readyState` is `OPEN`, but the agent server only starts reading inbound frames once the conversation's state lock is free, and `LocalConversation.run` holds that lock for the whole agent step. A frame sent to a socket that is not yet subscribed — and closed before the lock frees — is dropped. The pending bubble and the `conversation-state-<id>.draftMessage` copy are only cleared by the echoed user `MessageEvent`, so the text reappears as a draft.

Scope is the Canvas send path only: reuse the repository's existing direct-send fallback (`ConversationClient.sendEvent`, `POST /events` with `run: true`, already used in `sendMessage` when the socket is not open) for a send to a session socket that has not yet delivered any frame. Non-goals: the agent-server socket-subscription fix (OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6709, tracked in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6708), the cloud PAUSED/STARTING held-message flow, plan-mode sub-conversation delivery, and any retry/queueing beyond this single fallback. This fallback also covers agent servers without the SDK fix.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A message sent while the agent is running reaches the agent server and a user `MessageEvent` is recorded, even if the person leaves the conversation within a few seconds of sending (Steps to Reproduce above).
- [ ] After returning to the conversation once the agent has finished, the message appears in the conversation history, the composer is empty, and no "Sending…" bubble remains.
- [ ] A message submitted to a session socket that has delivered no frames yet is not carried by that socket; it still reaches the agent server through the fallback path.
- [ ] The message is recorded exactly once: no duplicate user `MessageEvent` when the fallback delivery and a later socket replay/echo both apply.
- [ ] A failed delivery is surfaced through the existing pending-message error state with its retry link within the existing pending-message timeout, instead of staying in "Sending…" indefinitely.
- [ ] Sending to an idle conversation still goes over the session socket exactly as before, with no regression in that path.

>    [`[subscribe_to_events()](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/f727ffaf2e0e6addc213037ae99ec459401c0e3f/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/event_service.py#L1038)`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/f727ffaf2e0e6addc213037ae99ec459401c0e3f/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/event_service.py#L1038) still dispatches its locking snapshot onto the shared default executor, bypassing the new conversation executor.
> 
>    Running the PR’s live benchmark with six WebSocket clients, conversation A finished in **6.4 seconds**, but conversation B’s event search **timed out after five seconds**. The tool deadlock is fixed; server-wide starvation remains. Route this snapshot through `_run_state_op` and cover the actual subscription path—the new test only checks execution-status reads.
> 
> 2. **[P2] Dead terminal recovery now waits for the command timeout.**  
>    [[Lazy checkout logging](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/6554/files)](codex://review?pr=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FOpenHands%2Fsoftware-agent-sdk%2Fpull%2F6554&path=openhands-tools%2Fopenhands%2Ftools%2Fterminal%2Fterminal%2Ftmux_pane_pool.py&line=248&side=right) removes an incidental pane-liveness check. Its replacement runs **after** command execution times out.
> 
>    Reproduced using ordinary terminal commands: start `(sleep 2; kill -9 $$) &`, let the shell die, then run `echo after` with `timeout=3`. Recovery took **0.51 seconds on base versus 3.83 seconds on this PR**. Default settings imply a 30-second delay; longer explicit timeouts can mean minutes. Detect errors from the existing tmux operations before entering the wait loop.
> 
> The broader checks were reassuring: **131 EventService tests, 41 SDK concurrency/interruption tests, and 6 real-tmux integration tests passed**, alongside targeted lifecycle checks. I found no public API/schema break or additional regression in context propagation, nested execution, interruption, resume, or fork.
> 
> The red SDK CI is a **real MCP validation-test failure**, contrary to the earlier bot review’s infrastructure diagnosis. I reproduced it on both base and head, so it is **pre-existing**, not caused by this PR.

issue.body:
## Bug Description
If you send a message to a conversation while its agent is running, the message can be lost. The bubble stays at "Sending…", nothing reaches the agent server, and the text later reappears as a draft in the composer.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `npm run dev` with a local agent server. Start a conversation and give it a task that runs for a while, with several tool calls.
2. While the agent is running, open the conversation, so that a new session socket opens.
3. Type a message and press Enter. The bubble shows "Sending…".
4. Within a few seconds, go to another conversation. Come back after the agent has finished.

## Actual Behavior
- No user `MessageEvent` is recorded, and no `POST /events` is made.
- The session socket `/sockets/session/{id}?after_seq=…` opens and sends 2 frames, but receives 0 frames for about 40 seconds.
- When you come back, the text is in the composer again. It is restored from `conversation-state-<id>.draftMessage`.
- Cause: the agent server subscribes a new session socket only after `_create_initial_state_sync` has the conversation's state lock. `LocalConversation.run` holds that lock for the whole agent step. Until then the server reads no inbound frames, so a frame still unread when the socket closes is dropped.

## Expected Behavior
A message sent to a running conversation is delivered, and the agent picks it up after its current step. This should hold even if you leave the page right after sending.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A message sent while the agent is running reaches the agent server, even if the person leaves the conversation right after sending.
- [ ] Canvas doesn't rely on a session socket that hasn't delivered any frame yet to carry a user message.
- [ ] Sending to an idle conversation still goes over the socket, as before.

## Related
The server side is fixed separately in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6709 (issue OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6708). This Canvas fallback also covers agent servers without that fix.

<!-- openhands-ai-triage:start -->
---
## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Reproduced against the running app (`npm run dev` with a local agent server) and confirmed against the send path: `sendMessage` in `src/contexts/conversation-websocket-context.tsx` delivers over the session socket whenever its `readyState` is `OPEN`, but the agent server only starts reading inbound frames once the conversation's state lock is free, and `LocalConversation.run` holds that lock for the whole agent step. A frame sent to a socket that is not yet subscribed — and closed before the lock frees — is dropped. The pending bubble and the `conversation-state-<id>.draftMessage` copy are only cleared by the echoed user `MessageEvent`, so the text reappears as a draft.

Scope is the Canvas send path only: reuse the repository's existing direct-send fallback (`ConversationClient.sendEvent`, `POST /events` with `run: true`, already used in `sendMessage` when the socket is not open) for a send to a session socket that has not yet delivered any frame. Non-goals: the agent-server socket-subscription fix (OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6709, tracked in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6708), the cloud PAUSED/STARTING held-message flow, plan-mode sub-conversation delivery, and any retry/queueing beyond this single fallback. This fallback also covers agent servers without the SDK fix.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A message sent while the agent is running reaches the agent server and a user `MessageEvent` is recorded, even if the person leaves the conversation within a few seconds of sending (Steps to Reproduce above).
- [ ] After returning to the conversation once the agent has finished, the message appears in the conversation history, the composer is empty, and no "Sending…" bubble remains.
- [ ] A message submitted to a session socket that has delivered no frames yet is not carried by that socket; it still reaches the agent server through the fallback path.
- [ ] The message is recorded exactly once: no duplicate user `MessageEvent` when the fallback delivery and a later socket replay/echo both apply.
- [ ] A failed delivery is surfaced through the existing pending-message error state with its retry link within the existing pending-message timeout, instead of staying in "Sending…" indefinitely.
- [ ] Sending to an idle conversation still goes over the session socket exactly as before, with no regression in that path.

issue.body:
### Operating System

Windows

### Installation Method

From source (`npm run dev` / `npm run dev:minimal`)

### Agent Canvas Version

main @ 2e81dd9f2 (mock mode)

### Bug Description

Follow-up to #19399. #19400 made the resume placement fallback in `groupEvents` read suffix-free agent timestamps as UTC, but the completed-resume visibility filter in `src/components/conversation-events/chat/messages.tsx` (`visibleSessions`) still uses `Date.parse(messages[0]?.timestamp)`, which reads them as browser-local time. #19399's acceptance criteria name this filter ("the completed-resume visibility filter and the group placement fallback agree on suffix-free timestamps"), and that box is still open.

The filter only runs while `hasOlderEvents` is true, so it hits conversations longer than the first history page (50 events). West of UTC, a completed resume with no `afterEventId` that started within the UTC offset of the oldest loaded event is hidden from the chat. East of UTC, a resume older than the loaded page shows at the top of it.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run method: `npm run dev:mock`, browser timezone `America/New_York`.

1. Open the mock `pagination-local` conversation (100 events, so "Fetching older messages" stays available).
2. Replace the loaded events with messages stamped `2026-11-05T18:32:35.376752` to `2026-11-05T18:39:10.417648` (UTC, no suffix, as Agent Server sends them).
3. Add a completed resume activity with no `afterEventId`, started at `2026-11-05T23:20:00Z`.

Script: [.pr/reproduce-resume-visibility.mjs](https://github.com/jaeminbird/OpenHands/blob/5157ff29e759d545aaf965b06b8381a62191933e/.pr/reproduce-resume-visibility.mjs) (Playwright, `before|after`).

### Actual Behavior

No "Resumed session" row. The filter compares 23:20Z with 18:32:35 read as New York time (23:32:35Z) and drops the resume, although the history is about 5 hours older than it.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jaeminbird/OpenHands/5157ff29e759d545aaf965b06b8381a62191933e/.pr/resume-visibility-before.png)

### Expected Behavior

"Resumed session" shows after the last saved reply, where `groupEvents` already places it.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a browser timezone west of UTC and older events still unloaded, a completed resume with no `afterEventId` that started after the loaded history is shown.
- [ ] East of UTC, a completed resume that started before the oldest loaded event stays hidden.
- [ ] Timestamps with an explicit offset keep their meaning; `afterEventId` anchoring is unchanged.

### Additional Context

Fix (one line: `parseDateAsUTC`, as #19400 used, plus a test for both timezones): https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/compare/main...jaeminbird:fix/messages-resume-visibility-utc . Both new tests (America/New_York, Asia/Seoul) fail on main and pass with the fix; the New York one passes on main under TZ=UTC. With the fix, the same script shows the row:

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jaeminbird/OpenHands/5157ff29e759d545aaf965b06b8381a62191933e/.pr/resume-visibility-after.png)

I'll open the PR once this is ready-for-dev.

## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Confirmed against `main` (2e81dd9f244d3d12407f4900e33e48963df0807d). The resume placement fallback in `src/components/conversation-events/chat/group-events.ts` already treats suffix-free agent timestamps as UTC via `parseDateAsUTC` (`src/utils/format-time-delta.ts`, the mechanism #19400 added), but the completed-resume visibility filter in `src/components/conversation-events/chat/messages.tsx` (`visibleSessions`) still compares `session.startedAt` against `Date.parse(messages[0]?.timestamp ?? "")`, which per ECMAScript reads suffix-free timestamps as browser-local time. The filter only applies while `hasOlderEvents` is true (history longer than the first 50-event page), so west of UTC a completed unanchored resume newer than the loaded history is hidden and east of UTC a resume older than the loaded page is wrongly shown — leaving #19399's criterion "the completed-resume visibility filter and the group placement fallback agree on suffix-free timestamps" open.

Bounded scope: in `messages.tsx`, parse the oldest loaded message timestamp with the existing `parseDateAsUTC` helper (the same mechanism `groupEvents` already uses), plus focused regression tests covering a west-of-UTC timezone (row shown) and an east-of-UTC timezone (row hidden). Non-goals: no change to `afterEventId` anchoring, initialization placement, pending/connecting resume visibility, or `groupEvents` placement; no change to how explicitly offset timestamps are interpreted; no Agent Server timestamp-format changes (owned by `OpenHands/software-agent-sdk`); no new UTC-parsing utilities — reuse `parseDateAsUTC`.

Priority `priority:medium`: this is the still-open acceptance criterion from the beta user report behind #19399 whose fix (#19400) shipped incompletely, and the failure is reproduced in the running product (`npm run dev:mock`) with before/after evidence. Not high: the trigger window is narrow — a completed unanchored resume plus history beyond the first page plus a non-UTC browser timezone.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With the browser timezone west of UTC (e.g. `America/New_York`), `hasOlderEvents` true, and a completed resume with no `afterEventId` whose `startedAt` is later than the oldest loaded suffix-free message timestamp, the "Resumed session" row renders in the chat at the position `groupEvents` assigns it — the completed-resume visibility filter and the placement fallback agree on suffix-free timestamps (closing the still-open #19399 criterion). Verified by unit tests runnable with `npm test` and/or the mock-mode reproduction from this issue.
- [ ] With the browser timezone east of UTC (e.g. `Asia/Seoul`), `hasOlderEvents` true, and a completed resume with no `afterEventId` whose `startedAt` is earlier than the oldest loaded suffix-free message timestamp, no "Resumed session" row renders.
- [ ] Timestamps with an explicit offset (e.g. `Z` or `+05:00`) keep their stated offset in the visibility comparison, so the visibility decision for such history is the same under any browser timezone.
- [ ] `afterEventId` anchoring, initialization placement, and pending/connecting resume visibility are unchanged when older events remain unloaded, and the existing chat suites (including `__tests__/components/conversation-events/chat/group-events.test.ts`) pass via `npm test`.

issue.body:
### Operating System

Windows

### Installation Method

From source (`npm run dev` / `npm run dev:minimal`)

### Agent Canvas Version

main @ 2e81dd9f2 (mock mode)

### Bug Description

Follow-up to #19399. #19400 made the resume placement fallback in `groupEvents` read suffix-free agent timestamps as UTC, but the completed-resume visibility filter in `src/components/conversation-events/chat/messages.tsx` (`visibleSessions`) still uses `Date.parse(messages[0]?.timestamp)`, which reads them as browser-local time. #19399's acceptance criteria name this filter ("the completed-resume visibility filter and the group placement fallback agree on suffix-free timestamps"), and that box is still open.

The filter only runs while `hasOlderEvents` is true, so it hits conversations longer than the first history page (50 events). West of UTC, a completed resume with no `afterEventId` that started within the UTC offset of the oldest loaded event is hidden from the chat. East of UTC, a resume older than the loaded page shows at the top of it.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run method: `npm run dev:mock`, browser timezone `America/New_York`.

1. Open the mock `pagination-local` conversation (100 events, so "Fetching older messages" stays available).
2. Replace the loaded events with messages stamped `2026-11-05T18:32:35.376752` to `2026-11-05T18:39:10.417648` (UTC, no suffix, as Agent Server sends them).
3. Add a completed resume activity with no `afterEventId`, started at `2026-11-05T23:20:00Z`.

Script: [.pr/reproduce-resume-visibility.mjs](https://github.com/jaeminbird/OpenHands/blob/5157ff29e759d545aaf965b06b8381a62191933e/.pr/reproduce-resume-visibility.mjs) (Playwright, `before|after`).

### Actual Behavior

No "Resumed session" row. The filter compares 23:20Z with 18:32:35 read as New York time (23:32:35Z) and drops the resume, although the history is about 5 hours older than it.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jaeminbird/OpenHands/5157ff29e759d545aaf965b06b8381a62191933e/.pr/resume-visibility-before.png)

### Expected Behavior

"Resumed session" shows after the last saved reply, where `groupEvents` already places it.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a browser timezone west of UTC and older events still unloaded, a completed resume with no `afterEventId` that started after the loaded history is shown.
- [ ] East of UTC, a completed resume that started before the oldest loaded event stays hidden.
- [ ] Timestamps with an explicit offset keep their meaning; `afterEventId` anchoring is unchanged.

### Additional Context

Fix (one line: `parseDateAsUTC`, as #19400 used, plus a test for both timezones): https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/compare/main...jaeminbird:fix/messages-resume-visibility-utc . Both new tests (America/New_York, Asia/Seoul) fail on main and pass with the fix; the New York one passes on main under TZ=UTC. With the fix, the same script shows the row:

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jaeminbird/OpenHands/5157ff29e759d545aaf965b06b8381a62191933e/.pr/resume-visibility-after.png)

I'll open the PR once this is ready-for-dev.

## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Confirmed against `main` (2e81dd9f244d3d12407f4900e33e48963df0807d). The resume placement fallback in `src/components/conversation-events/chat/group-events.ts` already treats suffix-free agent timestamps as UTC via `parseDateAsUTC` (`src/utils/format-time-delta.ts`, the mechanism #19400 added), but the completed-resume visibility filter in `src/components/conversation-events/chat/messages.tsx` (`visibleSessions`) still compares `session.startedAt` against `Date.parse(messages[0]?.timestamp ?? "")`, which per ECMAScript reads suffix-free timestamps as browser-local time. The filter only applies while `hasOlderEvents` is true (history longer than the first 50-event page), so west of UTC a completed unanchored resume newer than the loaded history is hidden and east of UTC a resume older than the loaded page is wrongly shown — leaving #19399's criterion "the completed-resume visibility filter and the group placement fallback agree on suffix-free timestamps" open.

Bounded scope: in `messages.tsx`, parse the oldest loaded message timestamp with the existing `parseDateAsUTC` helper (the same mechanism `groupEvents` already uses), plus focused regression tests covering a west-of-UTC timezone (row shown) and an east-of-UTC timezone (row hidden). Non-goals: no change to `afterEventId` anchoring, initialization placement, pending/connecting resume visibility, or `groupEvents` placement; no change to how explicitly offset timestamps are interpreted; no Agent Server timestamp-format changes (owned by `OpenHands/software-agent-sdk`); no new UTC-parsing utilities — reuse `parseDateAsUTC`.

Priority `priority:medium`: this is the still-open acceptance criterion from the beta user report behind #19399 whose fix (#19400) shipped incompletely, and the failure is reproduced in the running product (`npm run dev:mock`) with before/after evidence. Not high: the trigger window is narrow — a completed unanchored resume plus history beyond the first page plus a non-UTC browser timezone.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With the browser timezone west of UTC (e.g. `America/New_York`), `hasOlderEvents` true, and a completed resume with no `afterEventId` whose `startedAt` is later than the oldest loaded suffix-free message timestamp, the "Resumed session" row renders in the chat at the position `groupEvents` assigns it — the completed-resume visibility filter and the placement fallback agree on suffix-free timestamps (closing the still-open #19399 criterion). Verified by unit tests runnable with `npm test` and/or the mock-mode reproduction from this issue.
- [ ] With the browser timezone east of UTC (e.g. `Asia/Seoul`), `hasOlderEvents` true, and a completed resume with no `afterEventId` whose `startedAt` is earlier than the oldest loaded suffix-free message timestamp, no "Resumed session" row renders.
- [ ] Timestamps with an explicit offset (e.g. `Z` or `+05:00`) keep their stated offset in the visibility comparison, so the visibility decision for such history is the same under any browser timezone.
- [ ] `afterEventId` anchoring, initialization placement, and pending/connecting resume visibility are unchanged when older events remain unloaded, and the existing chat suites (including `__tests__/components/conversation-events/chat/group-events.test.ts`) pass via `npm test`.

issue.body:
### Problem or Motivation

Paper is meant to feel like an old newspaper, a book or a journal. Its pale cream page, rust accent and teal links read instead as a contemporary warm-minimal interface. #19593 tried grey newsprint with carbon ink and blue-black links; that lost the warmth: its page had less colour and less light than the current Paper, and its ink was close to neutral grey.

Old print is warm because paper ages: newsprint yellows, and letterpress inks print brown-black.

### Desired Behavior

Paper prints as aged newsprint:

- a yellowed page and one warm black ink, with every neutral a screen of that ink;
- primary actions in reverse (paper on solid ink);
- one spot red for links, focus and danger;
- dark olive, ochre and red status inks that read as text, and no blue in the interface;
- code, diffs and terminal output by ink weight: bold ink keywords, faded comments, literals in the spot and status inks.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Every Paper text role meets 4.5:1 on every panel surface, and the body-text contrast contract covers Paper.
- Control edges meet 3:1 and filled-button labels 4.5:1 on Paper surfaces.
- Standalone links stay distinguishable from primary buttons.
- Prism, Monaco and xterm palettes use the same inks and pass their contrast tests.
- Other themes look the same as before.

### Additional Context

Supersedes #19593, which is closed. Implemented in #19595, together with the warning-contrast fix for #19594.

issue.title: Session socket drops a message sent to a running conversation

labels.name: repo-08ff7f38
labels.description: For bugs, affecting nearly all users and degrading performance or UX.

labels.name: repo-08ff7f38
labels.description: Issue meets development readiness criteria

issue.body:
## Problem

A session socket (`/sockets/session/{id}`) opened on a conversation whose agent is running reads no client frame until the current step ends. `session_socket` awaits `event_service.subscribe_to_events()` before starting `_inbound_loop`. Subscribing builds the initial-state snapshot under the conversation's state lock (`_create_initial_state_sync`), and `LocalConversation.run` holds that lock for the whole agent step.

So for the length of a step (40 s in the case below) the socket sends nothing back and reads nothing in. If the client leaves meanwhile, the writer's close wins the race in `_inbound_loop`, and the person's message frame is dropped: no `MessageEvent` is saved.

## Seen live

During a Projects demo, two messages sent to running worker conversations never arrived. The browser log shows the socket open, 2 frames sent (the first frame plus the message), 0 frames received for about 40 s, and then a close. An identical send to an idle conversation was delivered.

## Expected

A message the client sent is saved and runs once the step ends, even if the client leaves first. A frame that arrives together with the close is still handled.

## Acceptance criteria

- Inbound frames are read from connect, not only after the snapshot.
- A message already taken is saved even when the socket closes before the state lock frees.
- Tests cover both cases, and they fail without the fix.

<!-- openhands-ai-triage:start -->
---
## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Verified in the code: `session_socket` awaits `event_service.subscribe_to_events()` before starting `_inbound_loop`, and subscribing builds the initial-state snapshot under the conversation's state lock (`_create_initial_state_sync`); `LocalConversation.run`/`arun` holds that lock across the whole agent step apart from its LLM-call release windows, so a client frame sent during a step is not read until the step ends. ## Problem

A client of the agent server that shows a pull request (for example a card that links the PR an agent opened) has no way to show whether that PR is open, merged or closed, or whether its CI is passing, without holding its own GitHub token. The agent server already holds the provider token and uses it for `GET /api/git/repositories/search`.

## Proposal

Add a general, read-only route beside repository search:

`GET /api/git/pull-requests/{owner}/{repo}/{number}` (optional `provider`, GitHub for now)

It should answer 424 when no provider token is configured, so a client can hide the CI line instead of showing an error.

## Acceptance criteria

- Open, closed and merged PRs map to the right `state`; `draft` is reported.
- Any failed check run or failing/erroring commit status gives `failure`; otherwise any unfinished one gives `pending`; none at all gives `none`.
- 424 without a token, 404 for an unknown PR, provider errors mapped like repository search.
- Unit tests for the service and the route.

## Expected

- `Retry-After` (and any other exception header) is present on 4xx and 5xx error responses.

issue.body:
### Problem or Motivation

The Agent Server is getting Projects in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6602. That PR adds a project record, a `project` tag on its conversations, coordinator wake-ups, project files and memory, and workers that are normal conversations. It sits behind the experimental feature `projects`, which is off by default.

Today the only UI for this is the Insider Canvas App (enyst/insider). Canvas itself shows just a project badge on conversation cards (#19495). Someone who runs the Agent Server without the App has no way to create a project, see its work, or find its files.

The split we're aiming for: **what the server stores, Canvas shows. Ways of talking to the coordinator (the Insider Cat's personality, a docked chat, voice) belong to Apps**, and they can move into Canvas once they've proven themselves.

### Desired Behavior

All of the following appears only while `projects` is on (Settings › Experimental). When it's off, `/api/projects` answers 404 and Canvas shows nothing project-related.

1. **Every project has its own coordinator.** It is a conversation that receives the project's updates, starts and steers workers, and answers the person. Without one, nothing wakes on worker updates and nothing routes follow-ups, so **creating a project always creates its coordinator too**.
   - Canvas's create flow asks for a name, a goal, a workspace, and optionally a worker agent profile. It calls `POST /api/projects` with `coordinator: {working_dir, agent_profile_id?, title?}`. The server then starts the coordinator conversation with the project: the given or active profile, the coordinator tools, the project tag, idle, and no first message. It answers 201 with `coordinator_conversation_id`. This shape exists in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6602 since 73513fdee.
   - Apps can bring their own coordinator instead. Insider creates its Cat conversation and passes `coordinator_conversation_id` (enyst/insider#44).
2. **Projects in the top-left navigation.** Add a new **Projects** item to the top-left menu, with a **+** icon that creates a project. The item opens the Projects list, which shows each project's name and goal.
3. **Project page**:
   - A **Coordinator** entry at the top that opens the coordinator in the normal chat view, with no persona.
   - A board of the project's other conversations, grouped by what they need from the person (needs you / working / done / resolved), using the attention grouping from `GET /api/projects/{id}/conversations`.
   - Resolve and Reopen on each card, using the same tag semantics as the resolved banner (#19494).
   - The project's files (`/api/projects/{id}/artifacts`): upload, preview for text files, and who made each one (the person or a conversation).
   - Add an existing conversation to the project, or remove one from it.
4. **In any conversation**: the project badge links to the project page. The server headers ("[Update from …]", "[Message from the person in …]") render as compact lines, with mention chips (`[Title](conversation:<hex>)`).

### What stays in Apps (not in scope)

The Insider Cat's personality and skill, a Cat chat docked beside other views with live cards, voice, PR links on cards, and project progress summaries.

### Acceptance Criteria

- With `projects` off: no Projects navigation item and no badge, and nothing breaks against an Agent Server without Projects.
- With `projects` on, against a live Agent Server built from OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6602:
  - **Projects** + creates a project together with its coordinator;
  - asking the coordinator for work starts workers, and they appear on the board grouped by attention;
  - Resolve and Reopen work;
  - upload a file, see it listed, and preview it;
  - open the coordinator from the project page.
- Paper theme screenshots in `.pr/`.

### Alternatives Considered

- **App-only Projects** would need an App backend service that doesn't exist yet (durable coordination when the browser is closed, macOS support, restart, an authenticated connection back to the Agent Server). Keeping the backend in the Agent Server and a plain UI in Canvas means Projects works with or without the App.
- **Projects without a coordinator** were rejected (see 1.).

### Additional Context

- Agent Server: OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6602 (`projects` flag since ffac6b57c; turn it on with `PATCH /api/settings/experimental/projects {"enabled": true}`)
- Experimental settings: #19503 / OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6609
- Canvas Projects branch: #19495

**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

> Note (issue author, after triage): the coordinator is no longer optional. Canvas creates it through `POST /api/projects` with `coordinator: {working_dir, …}`. This is the Canvas half of the Agent Server's Projects feature: Canvas renders what the server stores, behind the `projects` experimental flag. - [ ] While `projects` is on, the project badge on a member conversation card links to that project's page, and the project page's Coordinator entry opens the coordinator in the normal chat view with no persona.
- [ ] In a conversation, server sender headers ("[Update from …]", "[Message from the person in …]") render as compact lines, and `[Title](conversation:<hex>)` mentions render as links/chips to the named conversation.
- [ ] Paper-theme screenshots showing the Projects page, the project board, the artifacts area, and the flag-off state are saved under `.pr/`.

issue.body:
## Bug Description
If you send a message to a conversation while its agent is running, the message can be lost. The bubble stays at "Sending…", nothing reaches the agent server, and the text later reappears as a draft in the composer.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `npm run dev` with a local agent server. Start a conversation and give it a task that runs for a while, with several tool calls.
2. While the agent is running, open the conversation, so that a new session socket opens.
3. Type a message and press Enter. The bubble shows "Sending…".
4. Within a few seconds, go to another conversation. Come back after the agent has finished.

## Actual Behavior
- No user `MessageEvent` is recorded, and no `POST /events` is made.
- The session socket `/sockets/session/{id}?after_seq=…` opens and sends 2 frames, but receives 0 frames for about 40 seconds.
- When you come back, the text is in the composer again. It is restored from `conversation-state-<id>.draftMessage`.
- Cause: the agent server subscribes a new session socket only after `_create_initial_state_sync` has the conversation's state lock. `LocalConversation.run` holds that lock for the whole agent step. Until then the server reads no inbound frames, so a frame still unread when the socket closes is dropped.

## Expected Behavior
A message sent to a running conversation is delivered, and the agent picks it up after its current step. This should hold even if you leave the page right after sending.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A message sent while the agent is running reaches the agent server, even if the person leaves the conversation right after sending.
- [ ] Canvas doesn't rely on a session socket that hasn't delivered any frame yet to carry a user message.
- [ ] Sending to an idle conversation still goes over the socket, as before.

## Related
The server side is fixed separately in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6709 (issue OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6708). This Canvas fallback also covers agent servers without that fix.

<!-- openhands-ai-triage:start -->
---
## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Reproduced against the running app (`npm run dev` with a local agent server) and confirmed against the send path: `sendMessage` in `src/contexts/conversation-websocket-context.tsx` delivers over the session socket whenever its `readyState` is `OPEN`, but the agent server only starts reading inbound frames once the conversation's state lock is free, and `LocalConversation.run` holds that lock for the whole agent step. A frame sent to a socket that is not yet subscribed — and closed before the lock frees — is dropped. The pending bubble and the `conversation-state-<id>.draftMessage` copy are only cleared by the echoed user `MessageEvent`, so the text reappears as a draft.

Scope is the Canvas send path only: reuse the repository's existing direct-send fallback (`ConversationClient.sendEvent`, `POST /events` with `run: true`, already used in `sendMessage` when the socket is not open) for a send to a session socket that has not yet delivered any frame. Non-goals: the agent-server socket-subscription fix (OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6709, tracked in OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#6708), the cloud PAUSED/STARTING held-message flow, plan-mode sub-conversation delivery, and any retry/queueing beyond this single fallback. This fallback also covers agent servers without the SDK fix.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A message sent while the agent is running reaches the agent server and a user `MessageEvent` is recorded, even if the person leaves the conversation within a few seconds of sending (Steps to Reproduce above).
- [ ] After returning to the conversation once the agent has finished, the message appears in the conversation history, the composer is empty, and no "Sending…" bubble remains.
- [ ] A message submitted to a session socket that has delivered no frames yet is not carried by that socket; it still reaches the agent server through the fallback path.

issue.title: Session socket drops a message sent to a running conversation

labels.name: repo-08ff7f38
labels.description: For bugs, affecting nearly all users and degrading performance or UX.

labels.name: repo-08ff7f38
labels.description: Issue meets development readiness criteria

issue.body:
## Problem

A session socket (`/sockets/session/{id}`) opened on a conversation whose agent is running reads no client frame until the current step ends. `session_socket` awaits `event_service.subscribe_to_events()` before starting `_inbound_loop`. Subscribing builds the initial-state snapshot under the conversation's state lock (`_create_initial_state_sync`), and `LocalConversation.run` holds that lock for the whole agent step.

So for the length of a step (40 s in the case below) the socket sends nothing back and reads nothing in. If the client leaves meanwhile, the writer's close wins the race in `_inbound_loop`, and the person's message frame is dropped: no `MessageEvent` is saved.

## Seen live

During a Projects demo, two messages sent to running worker conversations never arrived. The browser log shows the socket open, 2 frames sent (the first frame plus the message), 0 frames received for about 40 s, and then a close. An identical send to an idle conversation was delivered.

## Expected

A message the client sent is saved and runs once the step ends, even if the client leaves first. A frame that arrives together with the close is still handled.

## Acceptance criteria

- Inbound frames are read from connect, not only after the snapshot.
- A message already taken is saved even when the socket closes before the state lock frees.
- Tests cover both cases, and they fail without the fix.

## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Verified in the code: `session_socket` awaits `event_service.subscribe_to_events()` before starting `_inbound_loop`, and subscribing builds the initial-state snapshot under the conversation's state lock (`_create_initial_state_sync`); `LocalConversation.run`/`arun` holds that lock across the whole agent step apart from its LLM-call release windows, so a client frame sent during a step is not read until the step ends. Separately, `_inbound_loop` discards a frame that completes together with the writer's close, and a `send_message` already in flight is abandoned when the loop returns on close, so the message is lost.

The live Projects-demo incident in this report (two messages sent to running conversations never arrived; an identical send to an idle conversation was delivered) is a real user-facing failure with unrecoverable message loss, so this is prioritized high.

Scope: the agent-server session-socket inbound path only. The fix must keep using the existing `_inbound_loop`/`_ConnectionWriter` plumbing and the existing `event_service.send_message` path, including its current run/rerun semantics for a message sent mid-step — no parallel inbound mechanism.

Non-goals: no changes to the legacy `/sockets/events/{id}` endpoint; no change to `LocalConversation` state-lock or agent-step semantics; no change to the session-socket frame protocol, snapshot behavior, or `after_seq` resume semantics; no TypeScript-client or Canvas changes.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] While an agent step is running on the conversation (state lock held), a client that opens `/sockets/session/{id}` and sends a message frame has that frame read from the socket immediately: an automated test asserts the frame is consumed while the lock is still held, not after the step completes. (This currently fails: reading waits for the snapshot behind `subscribe_to_events`.)
- [ ] When the client closes the socket after sending that frame — the close racing or preceding the lock release — the message is still persisted as a `MessageEvent` in the conversation's event log, and the conversation processes it (a run picks it up) once the current step ends.
- [ ] A message frame that completes together with the writer close in `_inbound_loop` (both observed in the same wait) is validated and persisted, not discarded.
- [ ] Existing inbound behavior is preserved: malformed frames still produce an `ErrorFrame` and keep the connection open, auth control messages are still ignored, and the session-socket suites in `tests/agent_server/test_session_socket.py` and `tests/agent_server/test_agent_server_wsproto.py` pass.
